**Repo:** [sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger](https://github.com/sawers-rellan-labs/zealtiger)

## Setup

**Purpose**: Load packages, source stage functions, fix the seed.

**Approach**: Functions live in `R/01_compile_map.R` … `R/04_summarize.R`
(see the spec). simcross 0.8 is already installed.

**Expected outcome**: A clean session with all helpers in scope.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(simcross)
library(furrr)
library(patchwork)

# Stage functions (defined per the specification)
purrr::walk(fs::dir_ls("R", glob = "*.R"), source)

set.seed(params$seed)
plan(multisession)

map_dir <- params$map_dir

fs::dir_create("results/n1400/figures")

# Diagnostics
cat("simcross:", as.character(packageVersion("simcross")),
    "| seed:", params$seed,
    "| target NILs:", params$n_nil, "\n")
```

### Input data — MaizeGDB consensus map

The Stage-1 input is the ten MaizeGDB consensus genetic-map files (map ids
1203637–1203646) in `data/maizegdb_consensus_map/consensus_chr01.txt …
consensus_chr10.txt`, fetched by `download_consensus_map.sh`. `data/` is
git-ignored, so the chunk below **runs the download script automatically if the
files are not already present** — making the notebook reproducible from a fresh
clone.

Each `consensus_chrNN.txt` is a tab-separated MaizeGDB *map_text* export: line 1
is a free-text title (skipped), line 2 the header, then columns `Locus`,
`Coordinate` (cM), `Bin`, followed by repeating 4-column blocks per assembly
(`<assembly>_gene_model / _chr / _start / _end`). `parse_consensus_v5()` locates
the **B73 NAM v5** block (`Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0_*`) *by name* — its column
index differs between files — and keeps `Locus`, `Coordinate` (cM), and the v5
`chr / start / end`.

```{r ensure_input_data}
# data/ is git-ignored: fetch the consensus map if it isn't already there.
chr_files <- fs::dir_ls(map_dir, glob = "*chr*.txt", fail = FALSE)
if (length(chr_files) < 10) {
  message("Consensus map missing in ", map_dir,
          " - running download_consensus_map.sh ...")
  stopifnot(system2("bash", "download_consensus_map.sh") == 0)
  chr_files <- fs::dir_ls(map_dir, glob = "*chr*.txt")
}
stopifnot(length(chr_files) == 10)
cat("Consensus-map files present:", length(chr_files), "in", map_dir, "\n")
```

---

## Stage 1 — Compile the maize map (v5 NAM)

### 1.1 Parse consensus files

**Purpose**: Extract (locus, cM, chr, bp) anchors from all 10 chromosome
files, using the B73 NAM v5 physical columns.

**Approach**: `parse_consensus_v5()` matches v5 columns by squished name
(robust to per-file column differences), drops rows lacking physical
coordinates, and sets `bp` to the v5 gene-model midpoint.

**Expected outcome**: One tidy tibble of raw anchors across chromosomes.

```{r parse_map}
map_files <- fs::dir_ls(map_dir, glob = "*chr*.txt")

anchors_raw <- map_files %>%
  purrr::map(parse_consensus_v5) %>%
  purrr::list_rbind() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(chr, bp)

# Diagnostics
cat("Files parsed:", length(map_files),
    "| raw anchors:", nrow(anchors_raw),
    "| chrs:", paste(sort(unique(anchors_raw$chr)), collapse = ","), "\n")
```

### 1.2 Enforce a monotone Marey map

**Purpose**: Remove map inversions (mismapped / paralogous loci) so cM is
non-decreasing along the physical axis within each chromosome.

**Approach**: `enforce_monotone()` sorts by bp and applies a running-max
filter on cM. Track how many anchors are dropped per chromosome — large
losses flag consensus-vs-v5 disagreement (often pericentromeric).

**Expected outcome**: A monotone anchor set + a per-chr drop report.

```{r monotone_map}
anchors_clean <- enforce_monotone(anchors_raw)
drop_report   <- report_map_qc(anchors_raw, anchors_clean)

saveRDS(anchors_clean, "results/n1400/maize_map_v5_clean.rds")

# Diagnostics
cat("Clean anchors:", nrow(anchors_clean),
    "| total dropped:", sum(drop_report$dropped), "\n")
drop_report
```

### 1.3 Thin to the marker grid + per-chr cM lengths

**Purpose**: Build the ~`r params$n_markers`-marker grid and the vector of
per-chromosome cM lengths that `sim_from_pedigree` needs as `L`.

**Approach**: `thin_markers()` allocates the quota per chromosome in proportion
to cM span and selects markers evenly in cM. `L` = max cM per chromosome from
the clean map.

**Expected outcome**: `marker_grid` (for cM↔Mb + optional `convert2geno`)
and `chr_cm_lengths` (the simulation input).

```{r thin_grid}
marker_grid <- thin_markers(anchors_clean, n_target = params$n_markers)

chr_cm_lengths <- anchors_clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(chr) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(L = max(cm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(chr)

saveRDS(marker_grid, "results/n1400/maize_map_v5_grid2500.rds")

# Diagnostics
cat("Markers retained:", nrow(marker_grid),
    "(target", params$n_markers, "; cap, not a guarantee)",
    "| total map length (cM):", round(sum(chr_cm_lengths$L), 1), "\n")
chr_cm_lengths
```

### 1.4 Marey QC plot

**Purpose**: Visual gate before simulating — confirm the cleaned map is
monotone and sensibly shaped per chromosome.

**Approach**: cM-vs-Mb scatter, clean anchors overlaid, faceted by chr.

**Expected outcome**: `results/n1400/marey_maps.pdf`. **Inspect before Stage 2.**

```{r marey_plot}
marey <- anchors_clean %>%
  ggplot(aes(bp / 1e6, cm)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.5, colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~ chr, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Physical position (Mb, v5)", y = "Genetic position (cM)",
       title = "Marey maps (monotone clean anchors)") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave("results/n1400/marey_maps.pdf", marey, width = 11, height = 8)
marey
```

---

## Stage 2 — Pedigree + simulation (no selection)

### 2.1 Build and validate the pedigree

**Purpose**: Define the BC2S3 NIL pedigree (final NIL = id 8).

**Approach**: `bc2s3_pedigree()`; validate with `check_pedigree()`. Selfing is
encoded as `mom == dad`, so a single parent is both "mom" and "dad" — the
default sex-consistency check cannot pass and we use `ignore_sex = TRUE`. Sex
is immaterial for autosomal maize.

**Expected outcome**: `TRUE` from the check.

```{r pedigree}
ped <- bc2s3_pedigree()
stopifnot(check_pedigree(ped, ignore_sex = TRUE))

# Diagnostics
cat("Pedigree rows:", nrow(ped),
    "| founders:", sum(ped$mom == 0 & ped$dad == 0), "\n")
ped
```

### 2.2 Pilot run (n = 20) — fail fast

**Purpose**: Confirm allele labeling + donor dosage before scaling.

**Approach**: Simulate 20 NILs. The validation metric is **donor dosage** =
donor cM summed over *both* haplotypes / (2 × total map cM); this is the
allele frequency and converges to the analytical BC2S3 expectation **0.125**.

> Note: this dosage is distinct from the *unioned* introgression span used for
> the size distribution. A locus is "introgressed" if **either** haplotype is
> donor, so the union fraction (≈ f₂ + f₁ ≈ 0.141) is higher than the dosage
> (f₂ + ½f₁ = 0.125). We validate the dosage; we report sizes from the union.

**Expected outcome**: Mean donor dosage ≈ 0.125 (within MC error).

```{r pilot}
total_cm <- sum(chr_cm_lengths$L)

sim_one <- function(i) {
  res <- simulate_nil(ped, chr_cm_lengths,
                      m = params$m_interference, p = params$p_escape,
                      donor_allele = params$donor_allele)
  res$segments$nil_id <- i
  res
}

pilot <- furrr::future_map(seq_len(20), sim_one,
                           .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE))
pilot_dosage <- purrr::map_dbl(pilot, "donor_cm_hap") / (2 * total_cm)

# Diagnostics
cat("Pilot mean donor dosage:", round(mean(pilot_dosage), 4),
    "| expected: 0.1250\n")
stopifnot(abs(mean(pilot_dosage) - 0.125) < 0.03)
```

### 2.3 Full simulation (n = `r params$n_nil`)

**Purpose**: Generate the full NIL set and collect donor segments in cM.

**Approach**: Parallel replicate simulation; tag each line with `nil_id`.
Donor intervals are unioned across mat/pat per chromosome.

**Expected outcome**: `segments_cm` (one row per unioned donor segment) and
`dosage_per_line` (the genome-wide validation).

```{r simulate_full}
sims <- furrr::future_map(seq_len(params$n_nil), sim_one,
                          .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE))

segments_cm     <- purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(sims, "segments"))
dosage_per_line <- purrr::map_dbl(sims, "donor_cm_hap") / (2 * total_cm)

# Diagnostics
cat("NILs simulated:", dplyr::n_distinct(segments_cm$nil_id),
    "| total donor segments:", nrow(segments_cm),
    "| genome-wide mean dosage:", round(mean(dosage_per_line), 4),
    "(expect 0.1250)\n")
```

---

## Stage 3 — Convert segments cM → Mb

**Purpose**: Map donor cM intervals to physical Mb per chromosome.

**Approach**: `segments_to_mb()` builds a monotone `cM → bp` interpolator per
chr from the full clean anchors (`make_cm_to_bp()`, linear, clamped) and
applies it to each segment's endpoints. We then assert no segment exceeds its
chromosome's physical length.

**Expected outcome**: `segments_mb` with `start_bp`, `end_bp`, `mb`.

```{r segments_to_mb}
segments_mb <- segments_to_mb(
  dplyr::select(segments_cm, nil_id, chr, start_cm, end_cm), anchors_clean)

assert_within_chr_length(segments_mb, anchors_clean)

saveRDS(segments_mb, "results/n1400/nil_segments.rds")
readr::write_csv(segments_mb, "results/n1400/nil_segments.csv")

# Diagnostics
cat("Segments converted:", nrow(segments_mb),
    "| median segment (Mb):", round(median(segments_mb$mb), 2),
    "| max (Mb):", round(max(segments_mb$mb), 2), "\n")
```

---

## Stage 4 — Distribution + summaries

### 4.1 Per-NIL summary

**Purpose**: Collapse to one row per line (including lines with zero donor).

**Approach**: `summarise_nils()` — total donor Mb, segment count per NIL,
filled to the full `n_nil` set so zero-introgression lines are represented.

**Expected outcome**: `nil_summary` + saved table.

```{r nil_summary}
nil_summary <- summarise_nils(segments_mb, params$n_nil)

saveRDS(nil_summary, "results/n1400/nil_summary.rds")
readr::write_csv(nil_summary, "results/n1400/nil_summary.csv")

# Diagnostics
cat("Mean total donor Mb/line:", round(mean(nil_summary$total_mb), 1),
    "| mean segments/line:", round(mean(nil_summary$n_segments), 2),
    "| zero-donor lines:", sum(nil_summary$total_mb == 0), "\n")
```

### 4.2 Distribution figures

**Purpose**: Show the introgression-size distribution.

**Approach**: (a) total donor Mb per line, (b) per-segment Mb, (c) ECDF of
segment Mb with median + 90th percentile annotated.

**Expected outcome**: Panels saved to `results/n1400/figures/`.

```{r distribution_plots}
med_total <- median(nil_summary$total_mb)
p_total <- ggplot(nil_summary, aes(total_mb)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_total, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Total donor genome per NIL (Mb)", y = "NILs",
       caption = sprintf("dashed = median (%.1f Mb)", med_total)) +
  theme_bw()

med_seg <- median(segments_mb$mb)
p_seg <- ggplot(segments_mb, aes(mb)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "darkorange") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_seg, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Donor segment size (Mb)", y = "Segments",
       caption = sprintf("dashed = median (%.1f Mb)", med_seg)) +
  theme_bw()

q90 <- quantile(segments_mb$mb, 0.9)
p_ecdf <- ggplot(segments_mb, aes(mb)) +
  stat_ecdf() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(segments_mb$mb), linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = q90, linetype = 3) +
  labs(x = "Donor segment size (Mb)", y = "ECDF",
       caption = "dashed = median, dotted = 90th percentile") +
  theme_bw()

# minor x-axis ticks (ggplot2 >= 3.5): 10 Mb on the segment panels, 50 Mb on the
# total-genome panel (~900 Mb). The tick-length theme() is returned alongside the
# scale so it is applied AFTER theme_bw() (which otherwise resets tick lengths).
minor_ticks <- function(width)
  list(
    scale_x_continuous(minor_breaks = scales::breaks_width(width),
                       guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)),
    theme(axis.ticks.length.x       = unit(6, "pt"),
          axis.minor.ticks.length.x = unit(3.5, "pt"))
  )

dist_panel <- (p_total + minor_ticks(50)) /
              (p_seg   + minor_ticks(10)) /
              (p_ecdf  + minor_ticks(10))
ggsave("results/n1400/figures/introgression_size.pdf", dist_panel,
       width = 7, height = 10)
ggsave("results/n1400/figures/introgression_size.png", dist_panel,
       width = 7, height = 10, dpi = 150)
dist_panel
```

### 4.3 Interference sensitivity (m = 0 comparison)

**Purpose**: Bound how much positive interference shifts the segment-size tail
(spec §8.2). The primary run uses simcross's default `m = 10` (strong positive
interference, biologically defensible for maize); here we re-run with `m = 0`
(no interference) and compare.

**Approach**: A second full `n_nil` simulation at `m = 0, p = 0`; overlay the
segment-size ECDFs and tabulate tail quantiles.

**Expected outcome**: `interference_comparison.csv` + an overlaid ECDF.

```{r interference_sensitivity}
sims_m0 <- furrr::future_map(
  seq_len(params$n_nil),
  function(i) {
    res <- simulate_nil(ped, chr_cm_lengths, m = 0, p = 0,
                        donor_allele = params$donor_allele)
    res$segments$nil_id <- i
    res
  },
  .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)
)
segments_m0 <- segments_to_mb(
  purrr::list_rbind(purrr::map(sims_m0, "segments")), anchors_clean)
dosage_m0 <- purrr::map_dbl(sims_m0, "donor_cm_hap") / (2 * total_cm)

cmp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(segments_mb, model = "default (m=10)"),
  dplyr::mutate(segments_m0, model = "no interference (m=0)")
)
cmp_summary <- cmp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_seg = dplyr::n(), median_mb = median(mb),
                   p90_mb = quantile(mb, 0.9), p99_mb = quantile(mb, 0.99),
                   max_mb = max(mb), .groups = "drop")
readr::write_csv(cmp_summary, "results/n1400/interference_comparison.csv")

p_cmp <- ggplot(cmp, aes(mb, colour = model)) +
  stat_ecdf() +
  labs(x = "Donor segment size (Mb)", y = "ECDF",
       title = "Interference sensitivity: segment-size tail", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave("results/n1400/figures/interference_comparison.pdf", p_cmp, width = 7, height = 5)
ggsave("results/n1400/figures/interference_comparison.png", p_cmp, width = 7, height = 5,
       dpi = 150)

cmp_summary
p_cmp
```

### 4.4 Crossovers per genome — RTIGER `crossovers_per_megabase`

**Purpose**: Provide the detectable-crossover statistics needed to autotune the
RTIGER rigidity parameter `r`. RTIGER segments the resequenced genome into
donor/recurrent blocks; each block boundary is a detectable crossover. With two
founders, every mosaic allele transition in the simulated NIL is exactly such a
crossover, so we count `mat + pat` allele transitions per diploid genome.

**Approach**: `n_crossovers_hap()` (already applied inside `simulate_nil`,
returned as `co_chr`) gives per-chromosome transition counts; `crossover_summary()`
reduces them to per-genome and per-Mb statistics. RTIGER's autotune wants the
**highest** CO/Mb across samples as a conservative input, so we report both mean
and max. The `m = 0` run bounds the value from above (no interference clusters
fewer COs, lengthening the per-sample tail).

**Expected outcome**: per-genome CO mean/max, CO/Mb mean/max, per-chromosome CO
counts, and the recommended `crossovers_per_megabase`.

```{r crossovers}
genome_mb <- sum(chr_phys_lengths(anchors_clean)$chr_mb)

co_genome <- tibble::tibble(
  nil_id = seq_along(sims),
  n_co   = purrr::map_dbl(sims, ~ sum(.x$co_chr$n_co))
)
co_stats <- crossover_summary(co_genome, genome_mb)

co_genome_m0 <- tibble::tibble(
  nil_id = seq_along(sims_m0),
  n_co   = purrr::map_dbl(sims_m0, ~ sum(.x$co_chr$n_co))
)
co_stats_m0 <- crossover_summary(co_genome_m0, genome_mb)

co_per_chr <- purrr::imap(sims, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$co_chr, nil_id = .y)) %>%
  purrr::list_rbind() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(chr) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_co = mean(n_co), max_co = max(n_co), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(chr_phys_lengths(anchors_clean), by = "chr") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mean_co_per_mb = mean_co / chr_mb,
                max_co_per_mb  = max_co  / chr_mb)

# conservative per-chromosome CO/Mb vector (max over samples) for RTIGER
co_per_mb_vector <- setNames(co_per_chr$max_co_per_mb,
                             paste0("chr", co_per_chr$chr))

readr::write_csv(dplyr::mutate(co_genome, co_per_mb = n_co / genome_mb),
                 "results/n1400/nil_crossovers.csv")
readr::write_csv(co_per_chr, "results/n1400/crossovers_per_chr.csv")

# Diagnostics
cat(sprintf(
  "Detectable CO per genome (m=10): mean %.1f (sd %.1f), median %d, range %d-%d\n",
  co_stats$mean_co_genome, co_stats$sd_co_genome, co_stats$median_co_genome,
  co_stats$min_co_genome, co_stats$max_co_genome))
cat(sprintf("CO per Mb (m=10): mean %.4f | max (conservative) %.4f\n",
            co_stats$mean_co_per_mb, co_stats$max_co_per_mb))
cat(sprintf("CO per Mb (m=0,  upper bound): mean %.4f | max %.4f\n",
            co_stats_m0$mean_co_per_mb, co_stats_m0$max_co_per_mb))
cat(sprintf("\n>>> RTIGER crossovers_per_megabase (genome-wide, conservative): %.4f <<<\n",
            co_stats$max_co_per_mb))
cat("\nPer-chromosome conservative CO/Mb vector (max over samples):\n")
print(round(co_per_mb_vector, 4))
co_per_chr
```

**Purpose**: Record parameters for reproducibility.

**Approach**: Write params + versions to JSON, including both interference runs
and the crossover statistics.

**Expected outcome**: `results/n1400/run_metadata.json`.

```{r metadata}
jsonlite::write_json(
  list(
    seed        = params$seed,
    n_nil       = params$n_nil,
    n_markers   = nrow(marker_grid),
    total_cM    = total_cm,
    genome_Mb   = genome_mb,
    simcross    = as.character(packageVersion("simcross")),
    primary     = list(m = params$m_interference, p = params$p_escape,
                       mean_donor_dosage = mean(dosage_per_line),
                       mean_total_mb = mean(nil_summary$total_mb),
                       mean_co_per_genome = co_stats$mean_co_genome,
                       max_co_per_genome  = co_stats$max_co_genome,
                       mean_co_per_mb     = co_stats$mean_co_per_mb,
                       max_co_per_mb      = co_stats$max_co_per_mb),
    sensitivity = list(m = 0, p = 0,
                       mean_donor_dosage = mean(dosage_m0),
                       mean_total_mb = sum(segments_m0$mb) / params$n_nil,
                       max_co_per_mb = co_stats_m0$max_co_per_mb),
    rtiger_crossovers_per_megabase = co_stats$max_co_per_mb,
    date        = as.character(Sys.time())
  ),
  "results/n1400/run_metadata.json", pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE
)
```

## Benchmarking RTIGER

**Purpose**: use the simulated NILs as ground truth to benchmark RTIGER's
ancestry/segment calling at the real **SNP50K** regime (λ ≈ 0.43×, ~71% missing).

**Approach**: `make_rtiger_benchmark.R` writes 100 NILs as RTIGER allele-count
files with known truth; `fit_rtiger.R` fits RTIGER (Julia backend, fork
`faustovrz/RTIGER@optimize-julia-core`) at a fixed rigidity; `score_rtiger.R`
scores the calls against truth. We report **two rigidities** so the choice is not
ad hoc:

- **r = 3** — the *minimum-CO-bias* point of the rigidity sweep (`docs/09`): of all
  rigidities tested it recovers the most crossovers. Reproduce with
  `Rscript fit_rtiger.R 0 3 0 4` then
  `Rscript score_rtiger.R --rtiger results/rtiger_benchmark/rtiger_out_r3/rtiger_result.rds`.
- **r = 8** — chosen *objectively* by RTIGER's autotune (`optimize_R`, initial
  r₀ = 50, minimizing the expected number of erroneous segments) on the SNP50K skim,
  and applied consistently to the MolBreeding target sequencing calls so all sources share one
  rigidity (`molbreeding_vs_skim.qmd`). Reproduce with
  `Rscript agent/autotune_rtiger_benchmark.R 0 50 "" 4`
  (writes `rtiger_out_auto/`, records the pick in `autotune_selected.txt`).

The trailing `4` is the Julia EM thread count: `threads = 4` cuts benchmark walltime
**~35%** on this machine versus single-threaded; fits are deterministic in the thread
count, so the tables below are identical regardless.

How r = 8 is obtained — the objective autotune call itself (kept `eval=FALSE`
because it needs Julia + the RTIGER fork, like the rest of this section; the tables
above are its scored outputs). The full script is `agent/autotune_rtiger_benchmark.R`:

```{r autotune_rigidity, eval=FALSE}
library(RTIGER); library(readr)
setupJulia(JULIA_HOME = Sys.getenv("JULIA_HOME")); sourceJulia()

ed   <- read_csv("results/rtiger_benchmark/expDesign.csv",  show_col_types = FALSE)
sl   <- read_csv("results/rtiger_benchmark/seqlengths.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
seqv <- setNames(sl$len, sl$chr_label)

# autotune=TRUE: fit once at the initial r0, run optimize_R (minimize the expected
# number of erroneous segments over a log-spaced rigidity grid), then refit at the
# winner. BOTH EM fits honour `threads`; optimize_R itself is analytic (single-thread).
# average_coverage and crossovers_per_megabase are left NULL so they are derived from
# the data — the same objective basis used on the real platforms (no truth peeking).
fit <- RTIGER(
  expDesign    = ed,
  outputdir    = "results/rtiger_benchmark/rtiger_out_auto",
  seqlengths   = seqv,
  rigidity     = 50L,        # initial r0
  autotune     = TRUE,
  max_rigidity = 2L^9L,
  save.results = FALSE,
  threads      = 4L,
  verbose      = TRUE
)
fit@params$rigidity   # -> 8  (autotuned rigidity; ~36 s / 100 NILs single-threaded)
```

**Expected outcome**: precision/recall by genotype class at both rigidities — the
hand-tuned minimum-bias r = 3 and the objective autotune r = 8.

```{r rtiger_benchmark, echo=FALSE}
# Headline results on the 100-NIL SNP50K benchmark (save.results = FALSE), scored
# against the simulated ground truth. Static (no Julia/RTIGER needed to render);
# r=3   -> results/rtiger_benchmark/scoring/        (min-CO-bias point of the sweep)
# r=8   -> results/rtiger_benchmark/scoring_auto_r8/ (objective autotune; matches both platforms)
marker <- tibble::tribble(
  ~r, ~state,                   ~recall, ~precision,
  3L, "0 homozygous recurrent",   1.000,     0.999,
  3L, "1 heterozygous",           0.974,     0.990,
  3L, "2 homozygous donor",       0.998,     0.997,
  8L, "0 homozygous recurrent",   1.000,     0.999,
  8L, "1 heterozygous",           0.974,     0.983,
  8L, "2 homozygous donor",       0.996,     0.997
)
segment <- tibble::tribble(
  ~r, ~class,                   ~n_truth, ~precision, ~recall,   ~F1,  ~FDR, ~boundary_kb,
  3L, "homozygous donor",            884,      0.987,   0.920, 0.952, 0.013,          85,
  3L, "heterozygous",                516,      0.962,   0.775, 0.858, 0.039,         127,
  3L, "TOTAL (donor present)",      1400,      0.981,   0.869, 0.921, 0.019,          85,
  8L, "homozygous donor",            884,      0.999,   0.887, 0.939, 0.001,          85,
  8L, "heterozygous",                516,      0.895,   0.773, 0.830, 0.105,         127,
  8L, "TOTAL (donor present)",      1400,      0.980,   0.861, 0.917, 0.020,          85
)
crossovers <- tibble::tribble(
  ~r, ~called, ~true, ~co_bias,
  3L,    19.4,  21.8,    -2.44,
  8L,    19.1,  21.8,    -2.71
)
knitr::kable(marker,
  caption = "Marker-level per-state recall/precision. Overall accuracy 0.999, ~0.36% uncovered at both r.")
knitr::kable(segment,
  caption = "Segment-level, reciprocal overlap >= 0.5, by rigidity.")
knitr::kable(crossovers,
  caption = paste("Crossovers per genome vs ground truth (true = 21.8).",
                  "r = 3 is the minimum-bias rigidity; the ~-2.4 floor is structural."))
```

**Takeaways**: marker-level genotyping is near-perfect (**99.9%**) at both
rigidities; donor-segment **precision ≥ 0.98 (FDR ≤ 2%)** — almost no false
introgressions; **recall ~0.86–0.92**, the missing ~8–14% being sub-Mb segments
below the SNP50K detection floor (`docs/09`), not a tuning shortfall. Boundaries
land within ~2 marker spacings (~85 kb; ~127 kb for het).

The two rigidities trade off as expected. **r = 3 minimizes crossover bias**
(−2.4 vs −2.7) and gives the best heterozygous-segment precision (0.96 vs 0.90),
so it recovers the most recombination — but no rigidity reaches zero bias, because
the ~2.4-CO deficit is the structural sub-Mb floor at λ≈0.43×, not a tuning choice.
**r = 8 is the objective autotune pick** and agrees with both empirical platforms,
trading a slightly higher CO under-count for marginally cleaner homozygous-donor
calls (precision 0.999, FDR 0.1%). RTIGER ran on the **fast path**
(`save.results = FALSE`, ~30 s / 100 samples single-threaded, ~20 s at
`threads = 4`) and was scored from the saved object.

## Production fit — real SNP50K population (per taxon)

The benchmark above is **100 *simulated* NILs** with known truth — it validates the
caller, it is *not* the population call set. The production fit (**Source 2**) runs the
same r = 8 RTIGER on the **real SNP50K skim**, grouped **by teosinte taxon** rather than
jointly: samples within a taxon share divergence from B73, so pooling the HMM emission
parameters is valid and gains power, while the largest group (Zx, 575) stays well under a
single ~1,400-sample joint EM (`fit_rtiger_by_taxa.R`; calls in
`data/rtiger_50K/calls_taxa_r8.csv`). After coverage QC (drop libraries with any
chromosome under 2·r covered markers) the fit covers **1,391 samples across five taxa**:

```{r rtiger_production_taxa, echo=FALSE}
# Per-taxon production fit on the real SNP50K skim, r = 8, save.results = FALSE,
# JULIA_NUM_THREADS = 4. Wall times from data/rtiger_50K/fits_taxa/run_summary.csv
# (regenerated 2026-06-12; the merge in fit_rtiger_by_taxa.R now accumulates all taxa
# instead of overwriting the file down to the last per-taxon invocation). Static tribble
# so this renders without the git-ignored data mount, matching the benchmark tables above.
# species per taxon code: donor_id prefix -> founder_group -> species, from
# /Volumes/rsstu/.../BZea/bzeaseq/sample_metatada.csv (Zx = mexicana races
# Chalco/Durango/Mesa Central/Nobogame; Zv = Balsas parviglumis; Zd/Zl/Zh as below).
prod <- tibble::tribble(
  ~taxon, ~species,                            ~n, ~seconds, ~status,
  "Zx",   "Zea mays ssp. mexicana",           575,   105.7,   "ok",
  "Zv",   "Zea mays ssp. parviglumis",        382,    68.6,   "ok",
  "Zd",   "Zea diploperennis",                253,    38.7,   "ok",
  "Zl",   "Zea luxurians",                    120,    25.7,   "ok",
  "Zh",   "Zea mays ssp. huehuetenangensis",   61,     8.7,   "ok"
)
prod <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  prod,
  tibble::tibble(taxon = "TOTAL", species = "—", n = sum(prod$n),
                 seconds = round(sum(prod$seconds), 1), status = "—"))
knitr::kable(prod,
  caption = paste("RTIGER production fit on the real SNP50K population, r = 8, per teosinte",
                  "taxon. Species from donor_id prefix -> founder_group in sample_metatada.csv.",
                  "Wall seconds single-machine, threads = 4. 1,391 samples total."))
```

**Takeaways**: the whole population fits in **~4 min wall** on one machine, no HPC —
flat-RSS scaling (≈1.2 GB + 3.2 MB/sample → ~5.6 GB at full joint size; §profiling).
Per-taxon mean donor dosage is **0.081**, consistent with the BC2S3 expectation
(≈0.125 before selection/drift) and the simulation truth. These calls are Source 2 of
the five-source cross-validation; the common-schema export lives in
`data/rtiger_50K/calls_common_schema.csv`.
